x-candidate-spans.text: `ckd_sodium_trial_bp.csv` — one comma-separated file with a single header row and 144 data rows.
The file is generated by `make_data.py` (Python standard library only, fixed random seed), which
rewrites the same file byte-for-byte when re-run.
**One row is one study visit for one participant: a single 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood
pressure average recorded at one of that participant's six monthly follow-up visits.**
A row is therefore not a person. Each participant owns six rows, one per visit, and those six rows
repeat the same participant identifier, trial arm, age, and baseline kidney function while the visit
number and the blood pressure value change. The repeated rows are time points on the same person.
| Quantity | Count |
| Enrolled participants (independent units randomised) | 24 |
| Follow-up visits per participant | 6 |
| Rows in the file (participants x visits) | 144 |
| Columns | 6 |
Every participant has a complete set of six visits numbered 1 through 6. There are no missing
values and no partial records.
Participants were randomised 1:1 into two trial arms, recorded in the `trial_arm` column:
| `trial_arm` value | Meaning | Participants | Rows |
| `usual_advice` | The clinic's usual dietary advice (control) | 12 | 72 |
| `intensive_counselling` | Intensive dietary sodium counselling (intervention) | 12 | 72 |
Arm is fixed at randomisation, so it is constant across all six rows belonging to a participant.
| Column | Type | Units / values | Varies within a participant? | Description |
| `participant_id` | text | `P01`–`P24` | No | Identifier for the enrolled participant. Repeats across that participant's six rows and is the only link between rows from the same person. |
| `trial_arm` | text | `usual_advice`, `intensive_counselling` | No | Randomised treatment assignment. |
| `visit_number` | integer | 1–6 | Yes | Which of the six monthly follow-up visits the row belongs to; 1 is the first monthly visit and 6 the last. |

| `systolic_bp_mmhg` | number | mmHg, one decimal place | Yes | The outcome: the 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure average recorded at that visit. Observed range across the file 105.5 to 155.6 mmHg. |
| `age_years` | integer | years | No | Participant age at enrolment. A stable participant characteristic. Observed range 48 to 77 years. |

| `baseline_egfr_ml_min_1_73m2` | number | mL/min/1.73 m^2, one decimal place | No | Baseline kidney function, the estimated glomerular filtration rate measured at enrolment. A stable participant characteristic, held inside the stage 3 chronic kidney disease band. Observed range 35.1 to 56.0. |
Column headers are lowercase words joined by underscores.
`make_data.py` invents the values from a fixed seed with this structure:
- Each arm is centred on a target level: roughly 134 mmHg for `usual_advice` and roughly 128 mmHg
for `intensive_counselling`.
- Each participant is given a stable offset from their arm's centre, drawn with a standard deviation
of about 9 mmHg. This is the spread between people.
- Each of the participant's six visit readings then varies around that participant's own level with
a standard deviation of about 5 mmHg. This is the visit-to-visit variation within one person.
Because the between-participant spread is the larger of the two, the six readings from one
participant sit closer to each other than readings drawn from different participants do.
`age_years` and `baseline_egfr_ml_min_1_73m2` are each drawn once per participant and copied to all
six of that participant's rows.
Compare `systolic_bp_mmhg` between the two levels of `trial_arm` (`usual_advice` and `intensive_counselling`).
The independent experimental unit is the enrolled participant. The column `participant_id` carries the value that

identifies it: each enrolled participant has one distinct `participant_id` value. Participants were randomised individually into one trial arm, so the participant is the unit that was assigned to a group.
The analysis is a two-group comparison of `systolic_bp_mmhg` between the two levels of `trial_arm`.
This protocol does not select, require, or exclude any particular statistical procedure.

x-candidate-spans.text: The analysis uses a single comma-separated file, `ckd_sodium_trial_bp.csv`, with one header row and
144 data rows.
**One row is one blood pressure measurement: the 24-hour ambulatory systolic average recorded at one
of a participant's six monthly follow-up visits.**
The file has six columns.
| Column | Type | Units / values | Description |
| `participant_id` | text | `P01`-`P24` | Identifier for the enrolled participant the measurement was taken from. |
| `trial_arm` | text | `usual_advice`, `intensive_counselling` | Randomised treatment assignment. |
| `visit_number` | integer | 1-6 | Which of the six monthly follow-up visits the measurement was taken at. |
| `systolic_bp_mmhg` | number | mmHg | The outcome: the 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure average for that visit. Observed range 105.5 to 155.6 mmHg. |
| `age_years` | integer | years | Participant age at enrolment. Observed range 48 to 77 years. |
| `baseline_egfr_ml_min_1_73m2` | number | mL/min/1.73 m^2 | Baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate at enrolment. Observed range 35.1 to 56.0. |
There are no missing values. All 144 rows are complete on all six columns, and every one of the six
visit numbers is present for every participant.
This was a single-centre nutrition trial in adults living with stage 3 chronic kidney disease.
Twenty-four adults were enrolled and randomised 1:1: 12 to intensive dietary sodium counselling and
12 to the clinic's usual dietary advice. Each participant then attended six monthly follow-up
visits, and a 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure average was recorded at each visit. Six
visits for each of 24 participants gives the 144 blood pressure measurements analysed here, 72 in
each arm.
The two arms were similar on the stable participant characteristics recorded at enrolment. Mean age
was 61.6 years in the usual-advice arm and 61.1 years in the intensive-counselling arm, and mean
baseline eGFR was 45.5 and 43.4 mL/min/1.73 m^2 respectively.
The outcome was the 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure average in mmHg. The two trial arms
were compared with an independent two-sample t-test on `systolic_bp_mmhg`, with each recorded
measurement entered as one observation. The sample size for the test is therefore the total number
of measurements, 144, split 72 and 72 between the arms. Group means and standard deviations were
computed on the same all-measurements basis, using the sample standard deviation with n - 1 degrees
of freedom.
The test was two-sided, and the difference is reported as intensive counselling minus usual advice,
so a negative difference means lower blood pressure under intensive counselling. Analyses were run
in Python 3 with pandas 2.0.3 and SciPy 1.9.1. The complete analysis is in `analysis.py` at the root
of the project, which reads the data file and prints every number reported below.
| Arm | n | Mean systolic BP (mmHg) | SD (mmHg) |
| Intensive counselling | 72 | 128.09 | 11.19 |
Mean 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure was 128.09 mmHg under intensive counselling and
134.02 mmHg under usual advice, a difference of -5.93 mmHg in favour of intensive counselling.
The independent two-sample t-test on all 144 measurements gave t = -3.62 on 142 degrees of freedom,
Intensive dietary sodium counselling lowered 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure relative to
the clinic's usual dietary advice. The mean was 5.93 mmHg lower in the intensive-counselling arm,
and the difference reached statistical significance at the conventional 5% level (p = 0.000413). A
reduction of roughly 6 mmHg in ambulatory systolic pressure is a clinically meaningful amount in
stage 3 chronic kidney disease, and these results support offering intensive sodium counselling to
this population.
